title: Minimum Operations to Make Subarray Elements Equal
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to make at least one subarray of size k have all elements identical.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to make at least one subarray of size k have all elements identical. Operations involve incrementing or decrementing any element by one.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 integers and 2 <= k <= len(nums).
One operation increments or decrements one chosen element by one.
Return the fewest operations needed to make every element of some length-k subarray equal.
hints: The median minimizes total absolute distance within a window.
Maintain window counts and sums over compressed values with Fenwick trees.
Insert and remove endpoints, select the median by cumulative count, and compute lower/upper distance from prefix sums.
Fenwick aggregates produce the exact L1 cost in logarithmic time for every sliding window.
editorial: Fenwick aggregates produce the exact L1 cost in logarithmic time for every sliding window.
